slot.brief: Find the interval in which a polynomial (factored form) is strictly increasing; test derivative sign.

stem: For $f(x)=(x-2)(x+1)^2$, in which interval is $f$ strictly increasing?

verdicts.working: f'(x)=3(x+1)(x-1), which is positive for x>1. Only (2,4) lies entirely in an interval where f is increasing.

working:
$f'(x)=(x+1)(x+1+2x-4)=3(x+1)(x-1)$
$f'(x)>0$ for $x<-1$ or $x>1$; $f'(x)<0$ for $-1<x<1$
Among the listed intervals, only $(2,4)$ lies wholly in an increasing region.

Independent check: f'(x)=3(x+1)(x-1), which is positive for x>1. Only (2,4) lies entirely in an interval where f is increasing.
solution:
$$f'(x)=3(x+1)(x-1).$$
Thus $f'(x)>0$ for $x>1$, so $f$ is strictly increasing on $(2,4)$.
